raw_plan.promise: Tally Pro gives an operations or customer success team one shared place to maintain customer-facing forms under its own branding.
raw_plan.orientation: Tally is a no-code form builder whose Pro plan supports shared team workspaces, removal of Tally branding, and forms hosted on a custom subdomain.
raw_plan.arc: In this single email, move the reader from seeing Tally as another form builder to recognizing a specific team-ready, branded form setup they can evaluate on the public pricing page.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: One email requires one complete commercial argument. Shared workspaces, branding removal, and custom-domain links combine into a concrete proposition for this audience: the team can jointly maintain customer-facing forms that present as its own. The public pricing page is the smallest useful next step because it lets a new buyer inspect all three required Pro capabilities before creating an account. No buyer pain, outcome, migration effort, or social proof is established, so the email should sell the documented operation rather than manufacture a failure story. The strongest distinct alternative is the native Notion route for the conditional subsegment that uses Notion. events.subject: Shared forms, under your brand
events.preview_text: Maintain customer-facing forms together with Tally Pro.
events.body:
Customer-facing forms should feel like they belong to the company behind them. With Tally Pro, your team can maintain intake and survey forms together, then present them without Tally branding and under your own branded link.

Tally is an online form builder. Its Pro plan lets you invite unlimited team members to shared workspaces, giving operations and customer success one shared place to maintain the forms customers see.

The same Pro plan removes Tally branding and hosts forms on a custom subdomain. Once that subdomain is pointed at Tally, you can use branded form links that keep the experience under your company’s name.

The official pricing page lays out these Pro capabilities in one place, so you can decide whether its collaboration and branding controls fit the way your team wants to run customer-facing forms.
